The purge path explains the orphaned files: [Posts.purge](/app/src/posts/delete.js:48) removes upload associations but never deletes the files. Topic purge calls that path for each post in [topics/delete.js](/app/src/topics/delete.js:54).

The likely fix is to capture a post’s upload paths before dissociation, then delete each file only after its reverse association set is empty. [posts/uploads.js](/app/src/posts/uploads.js:65) already has the per-post list and orphan check; it is also where the requested `deleteFromDisk(string | string[])` belongs. That function needs to reject other input types and keep resolved paths inside the upload directory.

The ACP option needs a default in [defaults.json](/app/install/data/defaults.json), a checkbox in [uploads.tpl](/app/src/views/admin/settings/uploads.tpl:9), and a label in the [English locale](/app/public/language/en-GB/admin/settings/uploads.json). One additional interaction needs review: [topic thumbnail deletion](/app/src/topics/thumbs.js:111) currently removes files unconditionally, including during topic purge, so it could bypass preservation or shared-file protection.

The [existing upload tests](/app/test/posts/uploads.js:213) verify dissociation on purge, but do not establish disk deletion, retention, or shared-reference behavior. I inspected code and tests only; the specialist instructions for this pass prohibited project source and test edits.

Implemented upload cleanup on post and topic purge. Files are deleted only after their last post association is removed; the new ACP **preserve orphaned uploads** setting retains them when enabled. `Posts.uploads.deleteFromDisk` accepts a path or an array, rejects other input types, and ignores paths outside the uploads directory.

ESLint passed, and the upload and thumbnail test files passed together: **56 tests**.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** Image uploads can create a separate `-resized` file in [src/controllers/uploads.js](/app/src/controllers/uploads.js:111). Upload tracking records the original filename in [src/posts/uploads.js](/app/src/posts/uploads.js:61), and purge deletes only that tracked path in [src/posts/delete.js](/app/src/posts/delete.js:68). Purging the last post that references the image therefore leaves the resized file on disk. Delete both variants once the original has no remaining post references and preservation is disabled, then cover that case in the existing upload tests.

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** `./node_modules/.bin/mocha test/posts/uploads.js test/topics/thumbs.js` exited 1 in the root setup hook: Redis connection refused at `127.0.0.1:6379` (0 passing, 1 failing). Start the configured local test Redis and rerun. `./node_modules/.bin/eslint --no-cache src/posts/delete.js src/posts/uploads.js src/topics/delete.js src/topics/thumbs.js test/posts/uploads.js test/topics/thumbs.js` exited 0.

This was a review only; no project code was changed.

Fixed post purge so that, when an upload has no remaining post references and preservation is disabled, it deletes both the original file and its `-resized` image. The upload test now checks that both files remain while another post references the image.

The reviewer’s exact Mocha command passed (56 tests), the flagged ESLint command passed, and `git diff --check` passed.
